extracted.intended_audience: SNSF program managers, Ambizione administrators, research funders, and evaluation/monitoring designers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for assessing the Ambizione funding scheme and for designing a monitoring system to trace grantees' career development and programme impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge transfer / win-back of knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowledge transfer or at least win-back of knowledge is attained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large shares of returnees and former grantees classified as incoming remain in the Swiss science system once their Ambizione funding has ended; Ambizione is suitable for generating knowledge transfer to Switzerland and benefits the Swiss science location as a whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attractiveness for returnees and foreign researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: Ambizione is particularly interesting for returnees and is attractive for researchers from abroad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The funding scheme’s suitability for researchers with limited mobility cannot be evaluated with certainty, but no evidence was found of marginalisation or exclusion of this group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation of women / gender balance
rubrics_metrics.description: Women’s participation in Ambizione should meet the SNSF target value and be monitored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shares of female grantees have been above the 35% target in most years (2013 exception). Success rates for female applicants have been lower than for males but generally remained above 20% (2013 exception). Recommendation: closely observe compliance with target values, regularly review the target, monitor trends (is 2013 an outlier?), and increase female representation on evaluation bodies (e.g., nominate more female committee members).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific independence of grantees
rubrics_metrics.description: Ambizione funding should promote grantees’ scientific independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most importantly, funding through Ambizione positively influences grantees' scientific independence (noting discipline-specific definitions). Scientific independence is tied to increased competitiveness on the academic job market and is a primary intended effect of the scheme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career impact and signalling effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Ambizione should have a significant impact on grantees' further careers and signal worthiness of support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receiving an Ambizione grant helps researchers attract further funding from the SNSF or other agencies and positively influences career trajectories both in Switzerland and abroad.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder satisfaction
rubrics_metrics.description: High satisfaction among grantees, hosts, and SNSF implementers is a success indicator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Satisfaction can be considered very high for almost all grantees; hosts and SNSF staff are generally happy with the scheme though minor optimizations are possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to hire scientific personnel (personnel support)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ambizione should enable grantees to hire scientific personnel (doctoral students/postdocs/technicians) as required by projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grantees expressed strong demand for personnel support; initial restrictions (no doctoral students/postdocs) were criticized and have since been changed. Duration constraints (e.g., three years) can prevent hiring PhD students who need time to complete their degrees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding duration adequacy
rubrics_metrics.description: The funding period length should be adequate for project goals and for hiring/supporting students/postdocs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grantees and hosts expressed a wish to extend funding from three to four years; SNSF supports the idea and is discussing implementation. Short funding periods reduce ability to hire doctoral students and finish projects within the grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and flexibility of funding regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations should be clear but allow flexibility (e.g., maternity leave, follow-up grants, budget allocation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grantees reported clear requirements and appreciated flexibility (e.g., postponing interviews due to childbirth). Some requested more budget flexibility (material/infrastructure). SNSF has adjusted rules (e.g., permitting hiring of doctoral students/postdocs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Portability and continuity of follow-up funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow-up grants and remaining grant resources should be portable when grantees take up new positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: a grantee was allowed to take remaining follow-up grant parts to a new university and hire a postdoc for 10 months; portability supports career moves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unequal treatment at host institutions & need for mediation
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor and address unequal treatment of Ambizione grantees across host institutions; SNSF should mediate when necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Difficulties stem from formal definitions of Ambizione positions at hosts and varying host requirements. SNSF currently mediates and may need to further develop this function or create an independent office for coordination, moderation, and troubleshooting between grantees, hosts and SNSF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host benefits from hosting grantees
rubrics_metrics.description: Hosting Ambizione grantees should broaden host institutes' scientific profile and add research activity and financial benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hosts are motivated by the researcher’s reputation and project. Financial benefits include overhead sharing and grantee-brought funds; grantees are seen as more independent than regular postdocs, leading to low support intensity for hosts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host disadvantages and resource constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and monitor host institutions’ disadvantages such as infrastructure needs or financial resource shortages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disadvantages observed in a small number of cases were caused by need to acquire additional infrastructure. 13% of hosts reported difficulties providing support due to lack of financial resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring objective: trace career development
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary objective of monitoring is tracing grantees’ career development after SNSF support ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitoring should enable assessment of Ambizione’s effect on competitiveness and long-term career outcomes; useful for ongoing programme improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of monitoring scope: holistic vs scheme-specific
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide whether monitoring is SNSF-wide (alumni system) or Ambizione-specific (focused).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Holistic approach embeds monitoring in an SNSF alumni platform (networking, identity forming). The focused Ambizione-specific approach reuses evaluation survey instruments and tailors monitoring to scheme characteristics. SNSF favors the latter for Ambizione.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring method: online surveys with longitudinal linking
rubrics_metrics.description: Use online surveys and ensure subjects can be linked across waves while preserving anonymity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Linking can be achieved by attributing a personal identification number to each grantee to relate answers while protecting anonymity; essential for tracing individual careers and detecting changes over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey design: cross-sectional vs longitudinal (recommendation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose between a cross-section survey (single survey per grantee) or a longitudinal/cohort design (multiple surveys per grantee).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation: longitudinal/cohort design with two survey waves per grantee (one at end of funding period and a second four years later) to measure short- and long-term impacts. Cross-section could be made compulsory (e.g., tied to acceptance of final reports) but provides less longitudinal insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohort timing and cadence of evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Define cohort composition and schedule for surveys and reporting (annual vs multi-year detailed reports).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define a specific point in time each year to conduct surveys. Because yearly cohort sizes are small, conduct descriptive data evaluation annually and more detailed evaluation and reporting every four years. Example table provided showing cohort waves and suggested timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Questionnaire length and content reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduce questionnaires to a small number of key questions relevant for career monitoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number of questions/topics will differ between first and second waves; the evaluation’s questionnaire can be used as a basis but should be streamlined for monitoring purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-wave survey topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus first-wave questionnaire (immediately after funding ends) on grantees’ experiences and immediate outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested topics: experiences as an Ambizione grantee; quality of integration into the host institute; collaboration with the host; support by scientific personnel; teaching activities during the funding period; grantees' plans for the future; future position or further funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second-wave survey topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus second-wave questionnaire (several years after funding ends) on career development and positions held post-funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested topics: career development after Ambizione funding ends; positions and employment situation after the end of funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data evaluation consistency and responsible parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure surveys are conducted and evaluated in an identical manner to ensure compatibility across waves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data evaluation can be performed by SNSF Administrative Offices or by an external firm. Identical survey and evaluation procedures are important to ensure comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to link subjects across waves
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitoring requires the ability to link subjects across waves to trace individual careers; otherwise tracing shifts over time is not possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of persistent personal identification numbers is recommended to enable longitudinal linkage while preserving anonymity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Option to make participation compulsory
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider compulsory participation in monitoring (cross-section) by linking survey participation to acceptance of final reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Making participation compulsory could ensure higher response rates for a single-wave cross-sectional approach, but would not substitute for the preferred longitudinal cohort design for measuring long-term impacts.
